chunks: And from him, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar al-Ansari, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no divorce except for one who intends divorce.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid divorce in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the legal efficacy of divorce (talaq) is strictly contingent upon the husband's conscious intention (iradah), distinguishing between mere utterance and actual legal effect. This principle, foundational in Shia jurisprudence, underscores that talaq is an act of will rather than a mechanical linguistic formula, requiring the husband to intend the dissolution of the marriage at the time of pronouncement. It serves as a critical criterion for determining the validity of divorce in cases of forgetfulness, error, or lack of awareness.
